content.title: About
content.content: Fruit juice drink is a non‑alcoholic refreshing beverage made from concentrated fruit juices diluted with water and sweetened to taste. It may contain natural flavorings and often has added vitamins and minerals to boost its nutritional value.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first commercial fruit juice drink appeared in the late 19th century in the United States.
There are more than 100 flavor variants, ranging from classic orange to exotic hibiscus and passion fruit.
Some brands use cold‑press technology to retain more vitamins.
Fruit juice drinks are frequently served in restaurants as “mocktails” – non‑alcoholic cocktail versions.
In several countries the drink is part of school nutrition programs because of added vitamins.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Citrus and berry juices are rich in vitamin C, which supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The water component helps maintain the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Fruit polyphenols and carotenoids protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Quick energy boost
items.content: Simple sugars in the drink are rapidly absorbed, providing an immediate energy lift.

items.title: Digestive support
items.content: Some versions are fortified with dietary fiber, which aids normal bowel function.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Most fruit juice drinks contain added sugars, which can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of tooth decay.

items.title: Fruit allergy
items.content: Individuals may experience allergic reactions to specific fruits used in the beverage.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Acidic drinks can irritate the stomach lining and erode tooth enamel with frequent consumption.

items.title: Preservatives and flavorings
items.content: Some brands add artificial preservatives that may cause sensitivity in susceptible people.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Fruit juice drink can be enjoyed chilled on its own, used as a base for non‑alcoholic cocktails, added to smoothies, or poured over desserts. To reduce sugar intake, it is advisable to dilute the drink with water in a 1:1 ratio.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the drink in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep it refrigerated and consume within 3–5 days. Discard the product if the packaging is swollen or if it develops an off‑odor.
